title: Chapter 9 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of audio, sound cues, spatialisation, Niagara particles, and combining effects!

questions.question: What is a Sound Wave in Unreal Engine?
questions.explanation: Sound Wave is the raw audio data imported from files like WAV or MP3.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Sound Cue?
options: To play sounds in a 2D space
To process and combine audio with logic nodes
questions.explanation: Sound Cues are node‑based graphs that mix, randomise, and modulate audio.

questions.question: To play a sound at a specific 3D location, use the _____ node.
questions.explanation: This node creates a temporary audio component at a world location.

questions.question: Which Sound Cue node picks one of several audio sources at random?
questions.explanation: The Random node outputs a single input selected at random.

questions.question: Attenuation controls how sound volume decreases with distance.
questions.explanation: Attenuation defines distance falloff, spatialisation, and air absorption.

questions.question: What is an Ambient Sound actor?
options: A placed actor that plays a Sound Cue in the world
questions.explanation: Ambient Sound actors place audio sources in the level with 3D spatialisation.

questions.question: What does an Audio Volume do?
options: Applies reverb and zone effects inside a region
questions.explanation: Audio Volumes change the audio environment (reverb, filter) when the listener enters.

questions.question: What is a Sound Class used for?
options: Grouping sounds for global mixing and ducking
questions.explanation: Sound Classes organise audio to apply volume, EQ, and ducking across multiple cues.

questions.question: What is a Sound Mix?
options: An asset that adjusts Sound Class volumes and effects globally
A node in a Sound Cue
questions.explanation: Sound Mixes modulate Sound Class settings (volume, pitch, EQ) dynamically, e.g., ducking.

questions.question: What is the primary VFX system in Unreal Engine 5?
questions.explanation: Niagara is UE5's advanced, modular particle system, replacing Cascade.

questions.question: What is the difference between a Niagara System and a Niagara Emitter?
options: A System contains one or more Emitters; an Emitter is a single particle type
An Emitter is a 3D sound source
A System is used only for GPU particles
questions.explanation: Emitters define particle behaviour; Systems combine emitters into a complete effect.

questions.question: Which module group runs once when a particle is born?
questions.explanation: Particle Spawn executes once per particle, setting initial properties like velocity and colour.

questions.question: GPU particles can collide with world geometry in the same way as CPU particles.
questions.explanation: GPU collision is more limited (depth buffer only); full physics collision requires CPU.

questions.question: Which module applies turbulence to particles?
questions.explanation: Curl Noise creates swirling, smoke‑like movement.

questions.question: How do you create a custom particle appearance?
options: Apply a custom material with particle nodes
questions.explanation: Materials can use Particle Color, dynamic parameters, and SubUV for custom looks.

questions.question: To make particles glow, set the material's Blend Mode to _____.
questions.explanation: Additive blending adds the particle's colour to the background, perfect for fire, sparks, and glows.

questions.question: What does the 'User Parameters' feature in Niagara allow?
options: Exposing variables that can be set from Blueprint at runtime
questions.explanation: User Parameters create dynamic inputs that Blueprints can modify, enabling reactive effects.

questions.question: How can you synchronise a sound with a Niagara effect?
options: Play Sound at Location and Spawn Niagara System at the same time in Blueprint
Attach a Sound Cue to the particle material
questions.explanation: In Blueprint, trigger both nodes simultaneously from the same event to sync them.

questions.question: Sound Cues can use modular nodes to vary pitch and volume randomly each time they play.
questions.explanation: Nodes like Modulator and Random can introduce variation.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using Sound Classes and Mixes?
options: Global control over groups of sounds (e.g., ducking music during dialogue)
questions.explanation: They allow adjusting volumes and effects per category without editing individual cues.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Niagara module group?
questions.explanation: Sound Attenuation is an audio feature, not a Niagara module group.
